name: NATS
summary: A subject-addressed messaging system whose Core NATS routes live publications and whose JetStream layer adds persistent streams, stateful consumers, replay, and replicated storage.

features.name: Hierarchical subject routing
features.description: NATS addresses messages with named subjects. Dot-delimited subject hierarchies and single- or multi-token wildcards let subscribers express interest in groups of subjects; the server maintains the active routing structure in memory.
benefits: Separates publisher addressing from subscriber location
Supports broad or narrow subscriptions without publisher changes
Makes authorization and monitoring patterns expressible over subject names
costs: Subject naming becomes part of the messaging contract
Wildcard subscriptions can widen delivery and authorization scope
Core NATS delivery is tied to currently connected subscribers

features.name: Persistent stream and consumer cursor
features.description: JetStream binds streams to subject patterns and assigns sequence numbers to stored messages. A consumer is a server-side stateful view with its own position; acknowledgements advance that position and unacknowledged messages may be redelivered.
benefits: Decouples publisher and consumer availability in time
Allows independent consumers to replay the same stream
Moves delivery-position bookkeeping into the server
costs: At-least-once delivery can require idempotent processing
Retention and consumer policy determine replayability
Consumer state adds operational lifecycle and recovery concerns

features.name: Configurable replicated stream storage
features.description: JetStream stream configuration selects memory or file storage, retention limits, and a replica count. The fixed server source exposes these choices in StreamConfig and routes persistence through a StreamStore abstraction.
benefits: Offers a durable history that survives server restarts
Makes storage, retention, and replication policy explicit per stream
Keeps the storage implementation behind a server-side interface
costs: Replication consumes additional storage and network capacity
Retention limits can remove data needed by a lagging consumer
Durability depends on deployment and configured replica policy

mathematical_views.question: Which subscribers are eligible to receive a publication for a given subject?
assumptions: Subjects are token sequences separated by dots
Wildcard matching is modeled as a relation from published subjects to subscriptions
The view describes routing eligibility, not authorization or delivery timing

mathematical_views.question: How do acknowledgements and redelivery evolve each consumer's position over a persistent stream?
assumptions: A stream is an ordered sequence of stored messages
Each consumer has an independent server-maintained cursor
The model includes retention and acknowledgement timeout transitions but does not prove external exactly-once effects

costs: Naming and wildcard scope require deliberate governance
Redelivery and retention create application-level recovery obligations
